notes: Phase 1 Step 3 (LLM API candidate labeling) against the pgadmin4_vuln source tree at sha 61fa8b1, which equals the CodeQL database creation sha; every CSV line number was re-checked against the tree, each entry's first evidence string is the verbatim source line at its location (read from the tree at generation time), and remaining evidence strings are verbatim lines or clearly marked cross-reference notes.
Single-pass labeling run: Pass 2 only (CWE-78 Command/Argument Injection), per exploration/detection.json target.pass=2, cwes=[CWE-78].

passes contains a pass_id=1 stub with zero entries solely to satisfy labels_schema.json 'contains' (requires a pass_id=1 element); pass 1 (path traversal) was NOT labeled in this run and must be labeled separately before any pass-1 query generation.

All 2209 candidate rows (sources.csv 2149 + sinks.csv 60) were dispositioned; 504 rows merged, yielding 1705 label entries (api+ast extraction facets of one call site; sink-side arg-ast/arg-api/shell_true/cmd_format/wrapper/construction facets of one exec site).

Labeling performed in-session by the agent's underlying LLM (glm-5.3); 8 batches (sinks 60 rows; http_request 699; request_param 46; json decode request-family 386; json decode non-request families 216; handler params 239; config 423; env 61 + cli 72 + internal_transfer 7); no external LLM API calls.

classification semantics: tp = confirmed genuine for the assigned role in this pass; fp = candidate rejected; candidate = plausible but unresolved, human review requested (kept for conservative recall); unknown = unused this run. API-label tp does NOT equal vulnerability ground-truth TP - none of the labeled exec sites is presumed vulnerable.

Signature flow_kind values follow labels_schema.json (param/argument/return/receiver/field/unknown): the extraction families map as http_request/request_param/config/cli/env attribute loads -> field, json decode returns -> return, handler parameters -> param, data-handing calls and sink command arguments -> argument.

No sanitizer entries: escape_dquotes_process_arg (bgprocess/__init__.py:157) only wraps arguments that already start and end with a double quote in #DQ# markers and is stripped again in the executor (:414) - not shell quoting; the double-quote doubling in misc/__init__.py:275 is partial escaping recorded in that sink entry's rationale, not modeled as a barrier; os.path.exists checks (misc/__init__.py:268, utils/__init__.py:338) verify existence, not shell safety; PasswordExec.get's SERVER_MODE NotImplementedError (passexec.py:26-28) is a deployment-mode gate recorded in the sink rationale; no shlex.quote/pipes.quote/shlex.join exists anywhere in the project source.

No PyVul ground truth, vulnerability patch commits, CVE descriptions or external security advisories were consulted; project source, CodeQL database, Augur installation and extraction artifacts were not modified.

entries.rationale: Popen(command, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, **kwargs) inside execute(): command = argv[1:] is the BatchProcess command list ([self.cmd] + self.args) handed over from the web process; kwargs['shell'] = True if _IS_WIN else False (:324) - on Windows the list is joined and interpreted by cmd.exe. The args originate from web-request JSON at the BatchProcess construction sites (backup:456/:465, restore:384, maintenance:238, import_export:326, views:2258, cloud rds/azure/biganimal/google) via _get_args_params_values. The only shell-relevant protection is escape_dquotes_process_arg (bgprocess/__init__.py:157: wraps arguments that already start AND end with a double quote in #DQ# markers, stripped again at :414) - double-quote handling only, no escaping of & | ^ % or embedded quotes. Genuine command-execution sink with request-reachable operands (Windows shell path); POSIX runs argv-list mode. Merged rows: arg (api), arg (ast) and the execute wrapper (:291).

Popen(cmd, **kwargs) Windows detached re-exec of [sys.executable] + argv: the executable is fixed (python interpreter, argv-list mode, no shell) and no attacker-controlled operand is executed at this site - but argv carries the unescaped batch-command list into the detached child which then runs execute() -> Popen(shell=True on Windows). Taint-transport step of the batch pipeline rather than a sink. Merged rows: arg (api), arg (ast).

BatchProcess.start() spawns Popen(cmd, ...) with cmd = [interpreter, executor, self.cmd] + self.args (:290-:291; Windows detached call at :330, POSIX call at :345, debug-mode get_process_output at :343): argv-list mode with fixed executables (python + process_executor.py) - self.cmd/self.args are data at this site, not the program being executed, and no shell is involved here. The web-request-derived command crosses the process boundary here and is shell-executed only in the child (see the process_executor.py:330 sink). Taint-transport step of the batch pipeline. Merged rows: arg (api), arg (ast) at :330 and :345 plus the start() wrapper (:281).
